2026-05-09T19:02:05.1929532Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1929887Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1930189Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1930668Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1931047Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1931514Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1945352Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1947198Z >
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1947972Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1948723Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1948919Z ### How to Use
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1949153Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1949676Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1950369Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1950521Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1950898Z # Discover what tools a server provides
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1951418Z <server-name> --help
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1951665Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1952023Z # Get detailed help for a specific tool (type, required status, description)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1952993Z <server-name> <tool-name> --help
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1953305Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1953656Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1954324Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1954896Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1955076Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1955312Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1955790Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1956279Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1957052Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1957863Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1958578Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1958756Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1959080Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs):
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1959650Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1960154Z safeoutputs --help                                 # list all safe-output tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1961015Z safeoutputs add_comment --help                     # show types and required params
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1961883Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1962984Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1963173Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1963497Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1964056Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1964527Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1965366Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966024Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966201Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966436Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966838Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1968242Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1970003Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1970158Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1970548Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1971364Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1972405Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1972711Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1973163Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1974235Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1976549Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1977018Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1977198Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1977936Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1978864Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1979023Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1979668Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1980561Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1981225Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1981640Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1982014Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983020Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983539Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983722Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983903Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1984674Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1985595Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1986525Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1987478Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1988375Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1988879Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1989026Z ### Notes
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1989213Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1989805Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1991168Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1992557Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1993788Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1994980Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1996059Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1996972Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1997751Z </mcp-clis>
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1998151Z <github-context>
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1998701Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-05-09T19:02:05.2010058Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2010751Z Run DollarLint against a fresh, bounded set of public repositories, persist the structured result, and publish a Discussion report.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2011616Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2011772Z ## Workflow
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2011975Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2012371Z 1. Use the `dollarlint-repo` MCP server first.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2013104Z    - Call `real_world_history` to inspect `reports/real-world-results.json`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2014194Z    - Use it to avoid repositories that have already been tested unless the manual input explicitly asks for a rerun.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2014937Z

2026-05-09T19:02:05.2033024Z    - Select up to `MAX_REPOS` repositories. Prefer a small, diverse set over a huge one. Default to 5.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2034375Z    - If the default pool is exhausted, pick other well-known public repositories with distinct ecosystems and conventional config files.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2035268Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2035428Z 3. Prepare and run.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2035908Z    - Call `real_world_prepare_corpus` with `clone: true`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2036773Z    - If it reports duplicates, choose replacements unless this was an intentional manual rerun.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2037866Z    - Call `real_world_run_corpus` with the prepared `corpusDir`, `cacheDir`, and `outputArtifact`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2039547Z    - Nonzero validation exit code 1 is expected when real issues are found. Treat crashes, missing output JSON, hangs, and unexplained warnings as higher-severity product signals.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2040692Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2040872Z 4. Triage the output.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2041369Z    - Inspect the DollarLint JSON output artifact with `jq`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2042524Z    - Separate parsing, validation, schema, coverage, warnings, crashes, performance, and output-contract findings.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2044301Z    - Decide whether each finding is a real third-party issue, expected test fixture data, SchemaStore mismatch, parser compatibility gap, confusing output/reporting problem, or DollarLint bug.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2046720Z    - Summarize product recommendations before finishing the run. Each recommendation must include a strength label of `high`, `med`, or `low`, based on frequency, severity, reproducibility, and expected user impact.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2048019Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2048203Z 5. Persist repository memory.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2049647Z    - Call `real_world_record_result` with the title, corpus, cache directory, command, output artifact, repositories, findings, product recommendations with strength labels in `productDecisions`, and follow-up notes.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2051519Z    - Also append a factual narrative entry to `reports/REAL-WORLD-TESTS.md` using the existing report shape.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2053345Z    - If files changed, request a pull request through the configured `create-pull-request` safe output. Keep the PR title concise and mention the structured result file.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2054411Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2054577Z 6. Publish the report.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2055248Z    - Request one GitHub Discussion through the configured `create-discussion` safe output.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2056278Z    - Title: use the run date and a short result summary, for example `2026-05-09 - 5 repo corpus`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2057047Z    - Body style:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2057446Z      - Use `###` and `####` headings only.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2058449Z      - Keep the summary, result counts, notable findings, and product recommendations with `high`/`med`/`low` strength labels visible.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2059641Z      - Put verbose per-file details and raw warnings inside `<details>` blocks.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2060668Z      - Include the tested repository table, DollarLint commit, output artifact path, and workflow run URL.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2062208Z    - If Discussion creation is unavailable, the safe output may fall back to an issue; mention that the intended destination was a Discussion.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2063119Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2064067Z Do not fabricate results. If cloning or validation fails before a meaningful corpus run, publish a short failure report with the blocker, partial artifacts, and the next concrete fix.
